g.text: Grounding as many small yes/no decisions
One candidate per pair of frames: is this interval inside the event?
PART II · METHOD
candidates: timestamp text of each frame pair (copied from the video prefix)
label yᵢ = 1 if the pair's middle time lies inside the annotated event (here 11–19 s)
Why pairs? The backbone merges every 2 consecutive frames into one set of visual tokens, so a pair is the finest unit the
LLM sees. One candidate = 2 / fps seconds: 0.5 s at 4 fps (evaluation), 1 s at 2 fps (training). A 2-min video at 4 fps → 240 candidates.
Loss 1: binary cross-entropy
each interval judged on its own, multi-label
(several can be positive):
L_BCE = mean over i of BCE(pᵢ, yᵢ)
Loss 2: soft IoU (stage 2, weight 2)
rewards covering the whole event, penalises
probability outside it, weighted by duration dᵢ:
L_IoU = 1 − Σ dᵢpᵢyᵢ / Σ dᵢ[yᵢ + pᵢ(1−yᵢ)]
Soft IoU matters: without it, mean grounding mIoU drops from 65.3 to 60.7.
VideoJev (arXiv:2610.18615), §2.2, Eq. (2)–(3) and Table 6; 20 intervals drawn for illustration
